headline_marked: [[The AI Senior Dev Dilemma]]: Am I Coding or Just Prompting?
headline: The AI Senior Dev Dilemma: Am I Coding or Just Prompting?
summary: A senior developer questions their role as AI handles much of the coding, raising concerns about skill development versus efficiency in modern software projects.
details: A senior developer, with five years of full-time experience, is using AI extensively for a new Angular project at work. Their manager is satisfied with the pace and timely ticket closures, despite the developer relying heavily on AI for code generation.

The developer grants the AI agent full access to the codebase but maintains strict control, reviewing all suggestions and never allowing direct pushes. They also use the AI for code reviews, significantly boosting efficiency and saving time.

Despite the project nearing completion, the developer admits to not having learned much about Angular, leading to feelings of being a 'fraud' or 'vibe coder.' This prompts a reflection on the actual value of manual coding versus AI-assisted development.

The core question revolves around the necessity of hand-typing boilerplate code for 'learning' when AI can generate it in seconds. The developer wonders if their ego is speaking, or if there's genuine value in the traditional learning process.

Ultimately, the consensus suggests that understanding the logic and taking responsibility for the implemented code is paramount. As long as the developer can vouch for the code's integrity and functionality, their role remains valid, regardless of the tools used.

headline_marked: [[China recovers first reusable rocket]] with unique sea-based net capture system
headline: China recovers first reusable rocket with unique sea-based net capture system
summary: China's Long March 10B booster was captured by a sea-based net system on an offshore vessel, marking the country's first controlled reusable rocket recovery and a new approach to booster retrieval.
details: China's state-owned rocket developer, CASC, successfully recovered an orbital-class booster for the first time. The Long March 10B rocket launched from Hainan Island, marking a historic day in China's space program.
The booster descended and guided itself into a four-legged frame on an offshore vessel. Tensioned cables captured the rocket as its engines shut down, leaving it hanging in midair.

This unique sea-based net capture method differs from SpaceX's propulsive landings. It reduces the need for heavy landing legs and minimizes fuel consumption during descent, optimizing payload capacity.
The Long March 10B is a medium-lift rocket with a payload capacity of approximately 16 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. Its first stage uses seven kerosene-fueled YF-100K engines.

This test flight validated key technologies like multiple engine restarts and high-precision navigation. CASC plans to optimize performance and complete the first stage reuse flight test by the end of this year.
The Long March 10B is part of a larger family, including the Long March 10A for future crewed missions to the Tiangong space station and a heavier Long March 10 variant for China's Moon program.
